A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ExPO-HM and retain the same research framework. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, equations, and appendices are readable and support reliable matching across additions, reorganizations, and renumbering.

before.justification: V1 reports original classification and reasoning results across three meme benchmarks, component ablations, warmup comparisons, and CDE analyses.

after.justification: V2 retains those original results and adds human evaluations, alternative-judge evaluations, calibration measurements, per-class results, and failure analyses.

M1.justification: The policy-manual SFT warmup, 50/50/50 GRPO curriculum, CDE reward design, and default parameters are retained. Corrections to the displayed GRPO loss sign and CDE cutoff notation do not establish a changed implemented training or inference procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use HatefulMemes, MAMI, PrideMM, and the Hatred rationale annotations for the same binary, fine-grained, and explanation tasks. The new human evaluations, calibration measurements, and error cases concern retained data and model outputs.

E2.justification: Matched comparisons retain zero-shot, SFT, DPO, GRPO, RA-HMD, LOREHM, and U-CoT+, with unchanged comparator membership in Tables 1–3. Additional LLMs in v2 serve as evaluators; the new diagnostic comparisons use existing baseline methods.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 changes the reported fine-grained metric from macro F1 to micro F1, although the original table values remain identical; this does not establish rerunning. New evaluation protocols add alternative judges, BERTScore, ECE with 10 bins, Brier scores, and randomized human coherence/helpfulness assessments by three annotators per example.

E4.justification: V2 adds judge and prompt sensitivity tests, human validation of explanation quality, calibration analysis, CDE hyperparameter sensitivity findings, per-class diagnostics, and three shared failure cases. These substantially extend v1's component/warmup ablations, CDE distribution analysis, and successful correction examples.

E5.justification: Appendix F newly reports inter-annotator reliability, with Krippendorff's ordinal alpha of 0.71. The three-seed, 60-point correlation analysis and its significance reporting are unchanged. V2 does not document an increased repeated-run count or add confidence intervals for the retained performance tables.

E6.justification: Tables 1–3 retain all numerical entries. V2 adds judge/BERTScore results, human coherence of 96% versus 100% and helpfulness of 1.6 versus 2.2 for GRPO versus ExPO-HM, calibration results, per-class scores, and failure examples. Table 12 gives 3B GRPO Brier 0.441 versus ExPO-HM 0.283; the 0.590 cited in Section 4.6 belongs to zero-shot.

T1.justification: The original CDE estimator and chain-rule derivations move unchanged from Appendix E to G. New Appendix H.2 derives confidence constraints and sample-level and dataset-level Brier bounds under an idealized binary CDE-maximizing policy, including Eqs. 16–31. V2 also corrects the GRPO loss expression and the final cutoff in Eq. 11.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims: an Explain-then-Detect system outperforming direct detection, the same three method components, and state-of-the-art binary, fine-grained, and reasoning performance. Additional validation supports these retained claims without redefining them.

C2.justification: V2 develops the interpretation of CDE as promoting calibration, discusses evaluator strictness and reproducibility, and explains hyperparameter failure regimes. Appendix J.2 newly identifies implicit hate and missing contextual/world knowledge as persistent failure conditions, with targeted annotation and retrieval proposed as future remedies. V1 primarily discussed successful cases and general deployment caveats.

D1.justification: V2 adds the complete Explain-then-Detect prompt, specifies one-time expert conversion of guidelines into policy manuals, documents CDE validation tuning and transfer, and supplies new evaluator identifiers and annotation instructions. Existing software versions, hardware, LoRA settings, training duration, and prospective code/artifact release arrangements remain unchanged.

R1.justification: V2 adds HelpSteer, cited for the human helpfulness rubric, and BERTScore, cited for explanation evaluation. The related-work narrative and novelty positioning remain substantially unchanged. Publication updates for HatefulMemes and RA-HMD refer to already cited works.

P1.justification: V2 corrects typos and terminology, updates affiliations, adds explanatory subheadings, and reorganizes Appendix B to separate ordinary prompts, policy-manual construction, and statistics. Most existing main-text prose and the overall narrative remain intact; the expansion mainly consists of new scientific material.

P2.justification: V2 adds evaluator, prompt-sensitivity, human-rating, calibration, and per-class tables, an annotation-interface figure, and a failure-case display. Original Figures 1–3 are retained, with sizing/layout adjustments. The six existing success cases move from Tables 9–10 to 15–16, and appendix table captions are repositioned above their tables.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens the central explanation-quality evidence through human ratings and checks across judges and prompts, addressing v1's reliance on one automatic judge and CDE. Per-class results and explicit failures also clarify applicability. The unspecified human-evaluation sample size, unreconciled macro/micro reporting change, and misattributed calibration baseline limit particular findings, but do not outweigh the broader corroboration and transparency.
